reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: We read every German string: Folge, the three inputs, 9 exam texts, 2 check lines, rule cards rc.trennbare-verben and rc.zeitangaben-inversion, strategy cards, instructions, situations, Leitpunkte, checklist, redemittel, endLines and cliffhanger. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: gist item, 3 × 5 inputItems, 3 × 4 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 12 reserve, 5 L3, 4 H3, 8 check and 2 proof items (92 authored items), plus the 8 perception items. Every sentence_building item's tiles were permuted by hand against its promptDe (Aussagesatz or W-Frage), and every error_correction was checked for alternative corrections. We ran the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js, on each typed item with its defensible alternative answers (number words, 24-hour clock, digits with „Uhr“, lower case). The exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: l3 5 items, richtig_falsch, signs 10–25 words; h3 5 items (4 here, reduced and scaffolded as allowed in a1.1), abc, 2 plays, 28–54 words; sp2 cards-ask, 2 topics; s2 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words. We recounted all 9 exam texts (signs 14–20 words, messages 29–37 words). Other checks: grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json (g.akk-personalpronomen a1.2-u09, g.koennen/Satzklammer a1.1-u08, g.imperativ-sie chunk from a1.1-u01); new-word load against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 ±10 %; 34 here, 17 productive); every learner surface against the cumulative lexicon, with a script built on scripts/course-v2/lib-validate/lexicon.mjs (knownForms + licensedForms) that walks promptDe, options, explanations, instructions, situations, strategy cards, titles and endLines; can-dos against registries/cando/a1.json; cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json; the story against u05, u06 and u08 and against a1.2-u04 (the Bürgerbüro unit); the plan against curriculum/a1-1.md §7, a1-1.json u07 and a1-2.md §4. Time arithmetic was recomputed (9–17 = 8 h; Bürgerbüro 8–12 vs course 9–12.30; Thursday 8.15 appointment vs course from 11; Bilal 14 Uhr + 1 h; Emre 14–20 Uhr İzmir and the call at 20 Uhr Leipzig).

LEX-02 has 11 ratchet: Nachmittag, Viertel, einkaufen, fernsehen, anrufen, frühstücken, Öffnungszeit, Termin, spät, Anrufbeantworter and Geschäft recur in fewer than 2 later units (F14). Skipped: ITM-08 (no caseSensitive item), CON-06 (no facts[] record, see F10) and the level-scope rules COV-1/4/5. All other rules pass, including ITM-09 (sentence-building orders), ITM-10, ITM-13, EXM-01…04, EXM-11, TXT-02/03/04 and LEX-01/03/05/07.

validator.notes: The validator is green, but three gaps still let findings through. (1) There is no cross-unit or cross-level story check (F01). (2) LEX-01 still does not walk item and instruction surfaces (r4-F04 rule unwritten; F05, and the reason the 26 „Bürgerbüro“ strings go unseen). (3) LEX-03 reads a separable verb as verb + particle and does not read authored fill_blank lemmas (F06).

verdict: Not exit-ready: 0 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR, 11 MINOR. We solved all 92 items (and the 8 perception items) blind, and every key is right. The sentence-building items accept every grammatical order their prompt allows. Every error correction accepts both repairs. The exam blocks match sd1.json in items, options, plays, word bands and a/b/c and R/F balance, and they are original. du/Sie is correct in every relationship. The Folge, the video chat with İzmir and the Thursday rescue by Herr Richter make a lively, well-timed day. Three things stop exit. (1) The whole LS2–LS3 errand, booking the Anmeldung at the Bürgerbüro, is the plot of a1.2-u04, which the plans route there. The authored a1.2-u04 contradicts u07 on every fact: Priya does not know about the Anmeldung („Zum Amt? Warum?“), they have not registered for months, the Bürgerbüro is open until 18 Uhr, and the room is 14 (F01). (2) The Sp2 Aufgabe that proves cd.a1.uhrzeit-tagesablauf never makes the learner ask or say what time it is (F02). (3) ls1-i05 marks „20“ wrong for Emre's 8 p.m. finish, although the unit teaches the 24-hour clock (F03). Nine of the eleven minors come from classes that the u04 exemplar raised before: structured input solvable by string matching, words allocated later on item surfaces, drills on receptive or missing lemmas, a Satzklammer preview on a rule card, Landeskunde without a fact or deviation, the genitive in the speaking instructions, and the validator's own false positives and ratchet.

scoreNotes.D: No wrong German on any model surface, and du/Sie is right everywhere (Priya–Emre–Arjun–Bilal–Olena–Sophie du; Herr Richter, the practice, the exam partner and every task Sie). It stays at 4 for six off-idiom lines (F11): „jede Woche Kurs, von Montag bis Freitag“, „Bitte, Sie fragen zuerst!“, the genitive „der Partnerin“, „am Donnerstag am Morgen“, q01's „es“ without an antecedent, and the unmotivated „nicht um drei“ in t7.
scoreNotes.N: 34 new words (17 productive), within 24–32 ±10 %. The production lines stay under the ceiling. It drops to 3 for three reasons. Later-level words are the unit's own setting and text-type nouns: Bürgerbüro (a1.2-u04, 26 strings), Schild (a1.2-u01), Praxis, Themen and Karten, unglossed on item and instruction surfaces (F01, F05). The Öffnungszeiten verbs aufmachen and zumachen have no lexicon entry, and receptive verbs are drilled as typed production (F06). The rule card previews möchte + infinitive (Satzklammer, u08), and the cliffhanger uses „dich“ (a1.2-u09) (F07). Two sub-rules of the new spine point are taught on the card but never practised: zuerst … dann and the connectors on Position 0 (F08).
scoreNotes.H: The day is believable and has a pulse: the late Folge with the Brötchen, Emre's 6-to-8 day in İzmir, the Bürgerbüro clash and Herr Richter's message that frees Thursday morning. It drops to 3 because the time half of cd.a1.uhrzeit-tagesablauf is claimed but never performed in its proving Aufgabe (F02). The three private voice messages also follow one template, and the S2 frame is constructed (F12).
scoreNotes.A: Every key is right, and every sentence-building and error-correction item accepts all defensible repairs. The distractors are plausible: h3-01's 9.15 and h3-04's halb sieben are well-aimed Viertel-vor/nach and halb traps. It drops to 3 because ls1-i05 rejects the 24-hour answer the unit itself teaches (F03, MAJOR). Also, LS2's four structured-input items can be solved without processing the inversion they train (F04).
scoreNotes.P: L3 (5 signs with location, 14–20 words, R/F 2/3), H3 (4 of 5 messages, reduced and scaffolded as a1.1 allows, 29–37 words, 2 plays, a/b/c 1/1/2), Sp2 (2 topics, cards-ask, Nora in Sie) and S2 (3 distinct Leitpunkte, 25–35 words, informal to a friend, model text 28 words plus a name slot) are exact to sd1.json. All texts are original. The strategy cards are honest. It stays at 4 for small points: the Sp2 situation asks the learner to „erzählen Sie von Ihrem Tag“, which goes beyond the one-answer format, and it uses a genitive (F11).
scoreNotes.K: The cast facts are right (Emre in İzmir in an Elektrogeschäft, online in the course; Herr Richter in the Sprachschule office; Frau Schulz as Kursleiterin; Olena, Sophie and Bilal), and the unit joins u06's cliffhanger and u08's Folge cleanly. It drops to 2 for a story contradiction with the later level: the Bürgerbüro Anmeldung is booked here and done again in a1.2-u04, with opposite facts (F01). There are also small breaks: Arjun's start time, the breakfast of the Folge's day, and spec.cast (F09). The plan's Landeskunde point has neither a fact nor a deviation (F10).
scoreNotes.E: Every instruction is ≤ 90 characters. Every endLine names the win. The perception prompts mask their quotes until answered (ItemView maskQuote), so the punctuation does not give the answer away. The 360 px Playwright walkthrough was not run in this round (it is the walkthrough reviewer's remit).

findings.problem: LS2–LS3 tell the Anmeldung plot: Priya and Arjun need a Bürgerbüro appointment for the Anmeldung, and Priya books it online for Thursday 8.15, Zimmer 12. The plans give this scene to A1.2 u04 (a1-2.md §4 „Anmeldung in der neuen Stadt: … Öffnungszeiten finden, einen Termin vereinbaren …“; a1-1.md l. 925 „Anmeldung im Bürgerbüro → A1.2 u04“), and the lexicon makes „Bürgerbüro“ a productive anchor of a1.2-u04. The authored a1.2-u04 contradicts u07 on every fact. Priya there does not know about the Anmeldung. The couple have not registered for months. The Bürgerbüro is open Monday, Tuesday and Thursday until 18 Uhr, while u07's whole dilemma is that it closes at 12 every day. The Anmeldung is in Zimmer 14. A learner who takes both levels meets the same errand twice with opposite facts, and u07's own appointment is never resolved: the cliffhanger jumps from Thursday 8.15 to the 11 o'clock class. „Bürgerbüro“ also stands on 26 strings of u07 (step title, options, prompts, explanations) and is glossed only in the three input texts.
findings.fix: Keep LS2–LS3 as they work: an office with morning-only hours clashes with Priya's 9–12.30 course, Herr Richter's message frees Thursday morning, and Priya books online. Give it an errand that no later unit owns. The plan's own Fokus line for u07 („Fokus Alltag: Sprechzeiten einer Arztpraxis lesen“) and the cast (cast.dr-sommer: Hausärztin von Priya und Arjun, which a1.2-u04's cliffhanger „Morgen rufst du bei Frau Dr. Sommer an“ already presupposes) point to a first appointment at Praxis Dr. Sommer. Gloss „Praxis“ in the input, as t6 already does. If you take this route, move t6 to another practice, so that the LS4 text does not move Priya's own appointment (the u04 r2-F06 class). Any other morning-only office works as well. Change the ls2 title, lines and sign, ls3-l06…l10 and the confirmation, ls2-i01/i02/i03, ls3-i02/i04/i05, ls3-s01, t4/sd1-l3-04, spec.situation and story.beat, and drop „Anmeldung“. In the rewrite, keep ls2-i03's explanation true to its source: Arjun reads the hours on the website, so „Auf dem Schild steht“ is wrong. lx.buergerbuero then stays at a1.2-u04, and a1.2-u04 needs no change.
findings.proposedRule: CON (new), with the LEX-01 surface walk of u04 r4-F04: a lemma that the lexicon allocates as a PRODUCTIVE anchor of a later unit must not appear on ≥ 3 learner surfaces of an earlier unit (setting-noun pre-emption). Failing fixture: a1.1-u07 with „Bürgerbüro“ on 26 strings against lx.buergerbuero @ a1.2-u04 (productive). The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: cd.a1.uhrzeit-tagesablauf: „Ich kann fragen und sagen, wie spät es ist, und erzählen, wie mein Tag abläuft.“ · learner card „Mein Tag – Uhrzeit“ → model „Um wie viel Uhr frühstücken Sie?“ · hintWords „Wie spät ist es?“ · moves []
findings.problem: The Sp2 Aufgabe proves this productive can-do, but none of its cards, model turns or moves has the learner ask what time it is or say it („Es ist halb acht.“). The learner's „Uhrzeit“ card is modelled as „Um wie viel Uhr …?“, which asks when something happens; that is cd.a1.zeitangaben, which the same Aufgabe proves. „Wie spät ist es?“ appears only in hintWords. Elsewhere in the unit the learner only recognises the phrase (MC ls2-p11, ls3-r03, c05, the gist item), orders it from tiles (ls3-p09) or reads it as redemittel (rm01, rm02). No micro-output, read-aloud or model turn produces it. The narration half is thin too: in Sp2 the learner answers one question per round with one sentence. So half of the can-do is claimed rather than performed. This is the r1-F07/r1-F13 class of the u04 exemplar.
findings.fix: Model the learner's round-1 card „Mein Tag – Uhrzeit“ as the time question („Entschuldigung, wie spät ist es?“ – Nora: „Es ist halb zehn.“). Give Nora a round-1 card that makes the learner tell the time, e.g. „Mein Tag – spät“ → „Wie spät ist es jetzt?“ → learner „Es ist Viertel nach zehn.“ (the AI partner accepts any well-formed time). Let the learner's model answer to „Wann stehen Sie auf?“ narrate a short sequence: „Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf. Um halb acht frühstücke ich, und um neun fängt der Kurs an.“ Add „Es ist halb …“ to hintWords. Optionally change the LS1 read-aloud to „Wie spät ist es? – Es ist halb neun.“
findings.proposedRule: ALL-02 (u04 r1-F07's rule, still unwritten): an Aufgabe that proves a can-do covers each function verb of the can-do (fragen / sagen / erzählen …) in its modelTurns, moves or Leitpunkte. If the can-do names a fixed phrase („wie spät es ist“), a learner model turn contains that phrase. Failing fixture: a1.1-u07 check.proofs[0]. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: promptDe „Emre arbeitet im Geschäft bis ___ Uhr.“ · accepted [„8“, „acht“] · exact „number“ · audio ls1-l04/l06 „Um zwei Uhr fange ich im Geschäft an. … Ich arbeite bis acht Uhr … Dann fahre ich nach Hause“ · checkItem(ls1-i05, „20“) → wrong; („zwanzig“) → wrong
findings.problem: Emre starts at 14 Uhr and goes home in the evening, so „bis acht Uhr“ means 20 Uhr, and „Emre arbeitet im Geschäft bis 20 Uhr.“ is the standard written form. The unit teaches exactly this 24-hour convention (ls2-s01 „„Von neun bis fünf“: von 9 bis 17 Uhr“, ls2-s04 „20 Uhr am Abend“), the signs use it (22 Uhr, 17 Uhr, 13 Uhr), and the plan's Landeskunde names it („24-Stunden-Uhr in … Terminen“). The v2 grader marks „20“ and „zwanzig“ WRONG. A learner who applies the unit's own Landeskunde gets a red X, so a defensible second answer is rejected (§9.4 MAJOR). No other typed time item has this problem: 6, 11, 12, 8.15 and 14 are unambiguous.
findings.fix: accepted [„8“, „acht“, „20“, „zwanzig“], acceptedWhy „20“: „24-Stunden-Uhr: acht Uhr am Abend ist 20 Uhr“. Explanation: „Emre sagt: „Ich arbeite bis acht Uhr.“ Das ist am Abend: 20 Uhr.“
findings.proposedRule: ITM-07: a typed exact:number item whose key is a clock hour from 1 to 12 either also accepts the hour + 12 (with acceptedWhy) or carries a reviewerConfirmed note that the time is before noon. Failing fixture: a1.1-u07 ls1-i05. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: ls2-s02 „Arjun: „Am Mittwoch arbeite ich zu Hause.“ Was ist richtig?“ → „Arjun ist am Mittwoch zu Hause.“ · ls2-s03 „„Am Abend sieht Arjun fern, und Priya lernt.“ Wer lernt am Abend?“ → „Priya“ · ls2-s01 „Wie viele Stunden sind das?“ · ls2-s04 „„Um neun Uhr fängt der Kurs an.“ Wann ist das?“ · ls1-s04 „„Am Nachmittag kaufe ich ein.“ Was macht Priya?“ → „Sie kauft Brot und Milch.“
findings.problem: LS2 trains V2 after a time phrase, but none of its four structured-input items needs that form to get the meaning. s02 is solved by the speaker label („Arjun:“) and by matching „zu Hause“. s03 is solved by finding „Priya lernt“ in the stem. s01 is arithmetic, and s04 is world knowledge (9 Uhr = Morgen). In ls1-s04 the key is the only option that repeats the stem's „kauf-“, and „Brot und Milch“ is an inference that the stem does not give. The u04 exemplar closed this class (r1-F26, r2-F03): there, the form decides the meaning (der/die/sind, wir/ich, möchtest du).
findings.fix: Let the verb–subject pair after the time phrase decide. ls2-s02: „Priya: „Am Mittwoch arbeitet er zu Hause.“ Wer ist am Mittwoch zu Hause?“ (Priya / Arjun / Priya und Arjun → Arjun, from „arbeitet er“). ls2-s03: „Priya: „Am Abend sieht er fern, und ich lerne.“ Wer sieht am Abend fern?“ (Priya / Arjun / Priya und Arjun → Arjun, from „sieht er“). ls1-s04: „Was macht Priya am Nachmittag?“ with options that all use a kaufen form („Sie kauft ein.“ / „Sie kauft nichts.“ / „Arjun kauft ein.“), or turn it into a „Wer kauft ein?“ item with an ich/sie contrast. Keep s01 and s04 as Uhrzeit items, or replace one with an order item („Welcher Satz ist richtig? Am Mittwoch arbeite ich zu Hause. / Am Mittwoch ich arbeite zu Hause. / Am Mittwoch zu Hause arbeite ich.“).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01 (role structured): the key must not be the only option that repeats a content-word stem of the quoted stem (verb stem or subject noun phrase). Failing fixtures: a1.1-u07 ls1-s04 (kauf-) and ls2-s03 („Priya lernt“ → „Priya“). The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: ls3-p02 „Das Geschäft ___ um acht Uhr auf. (aufmachen)“ · ls3-r01 „Der Supermarkt ___ um zehn Uhr zu. (zumachen)“ · ls3-mo „Wann macht der Supermarkt auf? Wann macht er zu?“ (no lx.aufmachen / lx.zumachen in any of the eight lexicons) · ls1-p03 „(fernsehen)“ → „sieht“ (receptive) · ls3-p03 „(anrufen)“ → „ruft“ (receptive) · learner model turn „Um wie viel Uhr frühstücken Sie?“ (receptive) · lx.uhr, lx.halb, lx.viertel, lx.spaet: role receptive
findings.problem: This is the r4-F02 class of the u04 exemplar. aufmachen and zumachen are the unit's verbs for opening hours, but they have no lexicon entry. They therefore get no card, no gloss and no recycling (LEX-02 cannot see them), and they do not count toward the 34 new words, although learners type their forms (ls3-p02, ls3-r01), build them (ls3-p07) and must say them (ls3-mo). LEX-03 passes only because „macht“ and „auf“ are each known on their own. Two typed er-form drills ask for receptive lemmas (fernsehen, anrufen), and the learner's Sp2 model turn and the lp2 cues use receptive frühstücken. The reverse gap exists too: the productive can-do cd.a1.uhrzeit-tagesablauf („sagen, wie spät es ist“) rests on Uhr, halb, Viertel and spät, which the lexicon marks receptive.
findings.fix: Lexicon owner: add lx.aufmachen and lx.zumachen to a1.1-u07, productive. To stay within 24–32 ±10 % (max 35), move one filler out of u07, e.g. lx.tag, which learners have met since „Guten Tag“ (u01), or lx.nach-hause. Make lx.uhr and lx.halb productive, and also lx.fernsehen, lx.anrufen and lx.fruehstuecken, which the unit drills; the productive share then stays ≥ 50 %. If the lexicon stays as it is, retarget ls1-p03 and ls3-p03 to productive verbs (einkaufen, anfangen), and change the Sp2 model turn to „Um wie viel Uhr stehen Sie auf?“.
findings.proposedRule: LEX-03 (the unwritten part of r4-F02): an authored fill_blank whose promptDe names a lemma in parentheses („(aufmachen)“) must name a lexicon lemma allocated at or before the unit with role productive. findings.problem: The spine point enters productively here with three sub-rules, and the unit practises only the first: time phrase or dann in position 1. No input line, item or model sentence has „zuerst“. None of the unit's 53 pool, reserve and check items trains the connectors on Position 0; only ls2-s03's explanation touches „und“. The spine's own errorTag connector-position is used nowhere, so ✗„Emre arbeitet, aber lernt Priya.“ is never repaired, and later units will treat the sub-rule as taught. Separately, the unit makes „der Morgen“ productive („am Morgen“ throughout) while it keeps using the adverb „morgen“ (tomorrow), which has run since u01 („Ich frage morgen im Kurs …“, t3 „Morgen sind wir ab 9 Uhr wieder offen.“, sd1-l3-03 „Morgen um 10 Uhr …“). findings.fix: In LS2, replace one of the three am/um fill-blanks with a sentence-building item: „Bilden Sie einen Aussagesatz.“ [zuerst / frühstücke / ich] → „Zuerst frühstücke ich.“ (also accept „Ich frühstücke zuerst.“). Put „zuerst … dann“ once into an input line, e.g. ls1-l10 „Am Nachmittag? Zuerst kaufe ich ein, dann lerne ich.“ (adjust ls1-s04's quote). Contrast the two words once, e.g. in the ls1 endLine or as a gloss: „morgen = tomorrow · am Morgen = in the morning“. Lexicon owner: give the adverb its own entry (u01, where „Bis morgen!“ starts).
